questions.question: Let [latex]f=y^x[/latex]. What is [latex]\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x\partial y}[/latex] at x=2, y=1?
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f &=y^{x} \\ \ln f &=x \ln y \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{f} \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} &=\frac{x}{y} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} &=y^{x}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)=y^{x-1} x \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\partial^{2} f}{\partial x \partial y}&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(y^{x-1} x\right)\\ &=y^{x-1}+x y^{x-1} \ln y \\ &=1^{(2-1)}(1+2 \cdot \ln 1)=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} f &=y^{x} \\ \ln f &=x \ln y \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{f} \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} &=\frac{x}{y} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} &=y^{x}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)=y^{x-1} x \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\partial^{2} f}{\partial x \partial y}&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(y^{x-1} x\right)\\ &=y^{x-1}+x y^{x-1} \ln y \\ &=1^{(2-1)}(1+2 \cdot \ln 1)=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]
